name: Jahzeel
overview: Jahzeel is a male figure from the tribe of Naphtali, known primarily as a son of Naphtali. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, indicating his place in the early history of the Israelite people. His descendants, the Jahzeelites, are noted in the book of Numbers, marking him as a tribal patriarch within Israel's genealogical records.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahzeel means 'G-d apportions,' reflecting a divine aspect in the meaning of his name. Another form of his name, Jahziel, appears in the Chronicles without a given meaning, but both names are proper names that were not directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jahzeel is a son of Naphtali, establishing his direct paternal lineage. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jahzeel holds significance as a tribal ancestor within the nation of Israel, representing the continuation of Naphtali's lineage. His mention among those who went to Egypt situates him in the foundational narrative of Israel's sojourn and eventual deliverance. The identification of the Jahzeelites in Numbers underscores his role in the tribal organization and heritage of Israel.
